FLAGGED: batch SR-13 is named in 2 official regulator alert(s) (as of 2026-10-18 11:52 UTC).
- COLDRIF (paracetamol, chlorpheniramine maleate, phenylephrine, sodium citrate) (batch SR-13) | Sresan Pharmaceutical | Adulterated: Contaminated: 48.6% w/v DEG | severity 5/5, Child Shield | WHO, "WHO Medical Product Alert N°5/2025: Substandard (contaminated) oral liquid medicines" (2025-10-13) https://cdn.who.int/media/docs/default-source/substandard-and-falsified/n5_2025_syrup-medicines_en.pdf?sfvrsn=652770c2_7 | Arkiv https://tiramisu.explorer.arkiv.network/entity/0x346f83d7a8bed1003081605c0ad3bc76fa953b4eefea2c8a0cc9128ed180fe54
- Paracetamol, Chlorpheniramine Maleate, Phenylephrine and Sodium Citrate Syrup (COLDRIF) (batch SR-13) | Sresan Pharmaceutical | Adulterated: Contaminated with diethylene glycol (DEG): 48.6% w/v, as reported by CDSCO | severity 5/5, Child Shield | WHO / CDSCO, "WHO Medical Product Alert N°5/2025: Substandard (contaminated) oral liquid medicines identified in India (diethylene glycol)" (2025-10-13) https://www.who.int/news/item/13-10-2025-medical-product-alert-n5-2025 | Arkiv https://tiramisu.explorer.arkiv.network/entity/0x13684cf7294dd7cf127818271db94fd570d932c61c5c74314b1217ffdadf8d3f
Confirm the brand and manufacturer on the pack match. If they do: stop using it, keep the pack, return it to the chemist, and see a doctor if it was taken.
